sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry without permeabilization confirmed surface display of FLAG-Iso1 and FLAG-Iso2 (L3, L4). Imaging flow cytometry quantified surface-to-cytoplasmic FLAG ratios and IFNL3-stimulated internalization kinetics, showing FLAG-Iso1 is more rapidly internalized than FLAG-Iso2 (L5, L6) — receptor trafficking function preserved and measurable.
sites.rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1–20 (landmark-authoritative); the mature N-terminus begins at residue 21 (R). Python confirms residue 20 = G and residue 21 = R in the canonical 520-aa sequence. Inserting the 3xFLAG after residue 20 places it at the extracellular N-terminus of the mature receptor, 207 residues from the TM boundary (228), satisfying all distance and topology constraints. L2 explicitly states UniProt-guided placement immediately downstream of the signal sequence, pinning the junction to 20/21; L3–L6 confirm surface display and functional internalization in multiple cell systems. L1 and L2 (PMC10052089) report synthesis of cDNAs encoding 3X-FLAG immediately downstream of the predicted signal sequence of IFNLR1 Iso1 and Iso2, with UniProt used to guide placement. Full-length, membrane-anchored constructs expressed under a doxycycline-inducible promoter in human cell lines and iPSC-derived hepatocytes.

sources.claim: To facilitate protein visualization and enable precise control of IFNLR1 expression, we synthesized cDNAs that incorporated a 3X-FLAG-epitope at the amino terminus of each IFNLR1 splice variant (referred to as FLAG-Iso1, FLAG-Iso2, FLAG-Iso3) ( Figure 1 , Supplementary Figure S1 ) under control of a doxycycline (dox)-inducible promoter [ 32 ].

literature_notes: All six ledger lines converge on a single site: the 3xFLAG tag inserted after the signal peptide cleavage site (residue 20/21 junction) at the extracellular N-terminus of IFNLR1. No internal loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or other positions are reported in the ledger. FLAG-Iso3 fails to traffic to the cell surface (L3, L4) but this reflects isoform-specific biology, not a distinct insertion site; no residue-level position is named for Iso3 and it is not a surface tag site. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named at residue resolution in the ledger.
